# Project index (code map) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A repository-only, hand-written `MAP.md` plus eight shards generated by `build/scripts/project-index.sh`, with a `--check` mode run by a new `project-index` workflow, so that routes, permissions, error codes, events, jobs, configuration, tests and switch markers can be found without a wide search and the index cannot go stale.

**Architecture:** One bash script (grep, awk, `git ls-files`; no new dependency) with a write mode and a `--check` mode. It reads the tree it is run in and hard-codes no module name. Output goes to `docs/superpowers/index/` (already excluded from generation). The script, its test and the workflow are repository-only: excluded in `template.json` and listed in the smoke script's `forbidden` list.

**Tech Stack:** bash 4+ (Git Bash 5.2 and ubuntu-latest), GNU grep `-E` only (no `-P`), awk (POSIX constructs only: mawk 1.3.4 on ubuntu must work), GitHub Actions.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-13-project-index-design.md` (decisions I1 to I9, Section 4 shard columns). Read it first. Where this plan and the spec differ, the plan's "Decisions this plan adds" are corrections found by a survey of the real code; the spec was amended for the three factual ones (12 endpoint files, `marker_line`, the job runs the script test).

## Global Constraints

- Header of every commit is a Conventional Commit of at most 72 characters (a hook rejects longer); end the message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Never `--no-verify`.
- Scripts start `#!/usr/bin/env bash` then `set -euo pipefail`; usage errors use `fail() { echo "project-index: $*" >&2; exit 2; }`; `.gitattributes` forces LF for `*.sh`. Only GNU `grep -E -I -r -n -l`; awk constructs must be POSIX (no `gensub`, no `match` with an array argument, no `\<`, no `length(array)`).
- Output is deterministic: `LC_ALL=C` for every `sort`, `grep` and `awk`; LF; strip `\r` from every input line; no timestamps; the file list comes from `git ls-files` when `<root>/.git` exists, else `find` excluding `bin`, `obj` and `.git`.
- Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` `--check` found a stale shard or a `MAP.md` problem, `2` usage or parse error (including a source that yields zero rows where the tree has some).
- Shard banner (line 1, exact): `<!-- Generated by build/scripts/project-index.sh; do not edit. Regenerate with: bash build/scripts/project-index.sh -->`; then a blank line, `# <title>`, a blank line, `Rows: N`, a blank line, a GitHub pipe table (header, separator, rows sorted with `LC_ALL=C sort`). A shard of more than 400 lines is an error in this plan's acceptance check (split it by module in the task that produces it).
- Never write a template-engine marker shape (a whole line starting `//#if`, `<!--#if`, `%%#if` or `#if`) in any file that ships; the new files here do not ship, and the banner is not a marker (`<!-- Generated`).
- A GateGuard hook asks for stated facts before the first Bash, Write or Edit of each file: state them and retry the identical call. Docker is broken locally; nothing here needs it.
- Every repository-only file this plan adds is excluded in `.template.config/template.json` (`sources[0].exclude`) and listed in the `forbidden` list of `build/scripts/template-smoke.sh`; the all-on drift check fails otherwise.
- Tests are written first and run red, then green.

## Decisions this plan adds

- **P1 Routes.** 12 `*Endpoints.cs` files hold 62 route mappings (21 GET, 30 POST, 6 PUT, 5 DELETE; 24 `RequirePermission`, 11 `AllowAnonymous`, 27 `RequireAuthorization`); 61 are documented, the 62nd is the JWKS route at `/.well-known/jwks.json`. There is no group-level auth; every route has exactly one of the three. The `/api/v1` base comes from `var api = app.MapGroup("/api/v1")` in `src/Host/*/Program.cs`; module extensions map on it; child groups (`MapMfaEndpoints` and others) take the prefix from their caller.
- **P2 Markers.** Use the whole-line rule `marker_line='^[[:space:]]*(\/\/|<!--|%%)?#(if|elseif|else|endif)([[:space:]]|\(|-->|$)'` (copy it from `template-smoke.sh`); one row per file. On the tree: 618 lines in 59 files; kinds `//`, `<!--`, `%%`, bare `#`; expressions `(notifications)`, `(includeSample)`, `(caching == "redis")`, `(notifications && includeSample)`, `(includeSample && notifications)`; strip a trailing `-->`.
- **P3 Errors.** Two tables in `errors.md`: declared codes (57 on the tree: Auth 43, Notifications 8, Sample 3, Pagination 3) from `*Errors.cs` (the code is the first string literal after `Error.<Factory>(`, on the same or the next line, or a `const string …Code` resolved in the same file), and resource-only keys (14: neutral `.resx` keys with no declaration, such as `validation.failed` and `http.404`). HTTP status comes from the factory: Validation 400, Unauthorized 401, Forbidden 403, NotFound 404, Conflict 409, Failure 500, Unavailable 503; a resource-only key `http.NNN` has status NNN, otherwise `-`. Resource key equals the code.
- **P4 Events.** 11 events (`record …IntegrationEvent … : IIntegrationEvent`, ten in `src/Modules/Auth/*.Contracts/IntegrationEvents/`, one in `Application.Common/Auditing`), 11 handlers (`: IIntegrationEventHandler<Event>`, the base list may continue on the line after the class name), 11 publish call sites in 10 files (`PublishAsync(` with `new <Event>(`). The Audit event is published by a building block, shown as such. Scan `src/` only.
- **P5 Jobs.** 15 job names: `AddRecurringJob<X>()` (10 in modules) resolves X's `Name` (`JobName` constant, `Name => "…"`), plus `IdempotencyCleanupJob`, plus `<Ctx>OutboxCleanup` for each `AddOutbox<<Ctx>DbContext>` (2) and `<Ctx>InboxCleanup` for each `AddInbox<<Ctx>DbContext>` (2). Config keys are `Jobs:{Name}:Enabled` and `Jobs:{Name}:Interval`.
- **P6 Config.** 15 top-level sections of `src/Host/*/appsettings.json` (skip marker lines; regex `^  "[A-Za-z]+":`). Owner: the project of the file declaring `const string SectionName = "<Section>…"` (first segment; several owners joined with `, `); the fixed Host allowlist is `Serilog`, `AllowedHosts`, `Kestrel`; anything else is `unassigned` and is an exit-2 error naming the section. Documented in: files among `docs/services/api.md`, `docs/modules/*.md`, `docs/building-blocks/*.md` that contain `### \`Section` or a table row starting `` | `Section ``; none is `-`, not an error.
- **P7 Tests.** Table 1: per test project, per first-level folder: source area (module if `src/Modules/<Folder>` exists; else the unique `src/BuildingBlocks/*` directory whose name contains `.<Folder>.` or ends `.<Folder>`; else `cross-cutting`), file count; a project without folders is one row `(flat)`. Table 2: name pairs `Foo.cs` (in `src/`, excluding `Migrations`, `bin`, `obj`) with `FooTests.cs` (in `tests/`) only when both basenames are unique (about 25 percent of sources pair); the number of skipped ambiguous names is stated in a line above the table.
- **P8 Checks and wiring.** The `project-index` job runs the script test, then `--check`. `ci.yml` is not touched (it ships). The repository-only workflow is `.github/workflows/project-index.yml`, modelled on `template-matrix.yml` (same triggers, permissions, concurrency, env, `actions/checkout@v7` with `persist-credentials: false`; no setup-dotnet). Making `project-index` a required check is the owner's action, reported in the final summary, not done here.
- **P9 No ADR.** A repository-only tool with a reversible design needs no ADR; the spec is the record.

## Review Focus

Each line is pinned by a test in the task that owns the code (named in brackets).

1. A Windows working copy with CRLF line endings must give the same output as LF, so `--check` passes on both [Task 1: a CRLF fixture file in the determinism case].
2. A new `*Endpoints.cs` file whose routes use a shape the parser does not know must fail with exit 2 naming the file, not silently emit fewer rows [Task 2].
3. A child route group (extension method on `RouteGroupBuilder`) takes its prefix from the caller, and a root route `"/"` never produces `//` [Task 2].
4. A tree without a module (a generated project with a switch off) yields no rows for it and no error [Task 2, module-absent case].
5. A deleted shard, or an extra shard that `MAP.md` does not name, makes `--check` exit 1 naming it [Task 1].
6. Untracked or ignored files (`bin/`, `obj/`, local scratch with markers) must not change the output: the file list comes from `git ls-files` [Task 1: a fixture git repository with an untracked file].

### Task 1: Generator skeleton, markers shard, `MAP.md` checks, test harness

**Files:**
- Create: `build/scripts/project-index.sh` (executable bit set in git: `git update-index --chmod=+x`)
- Create: `build/scripts/tests/project-index.test.sh`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces (used by Tasks 2 to 6): the CLI `project-index.sh [--check] [--root DIR] [--out DIR]` (defaults: root is two levels above the script; out is `<root>/docs/superpowers/index`); `list_files` (relative paths, sorted); one function per shard `emit_<name>` that prints that shard's table rows, one `|`-separated record per line with fields in the spec's column order, *unsorted*; `write_shard <name> <title> <header-row> <rows-file>` that adds the banner, `Rows: N`, the separator and the sorted rows; `fail_parse <message>` (exit 2); `need_rows <shard> <count>` (exit 2 when `<count>` is zero and the tree has a source for it); `check_map` (the three `MAP.md` rules below).
- The shard names, in the order `MAP.md` must list them: `routes permissions errors events jobs config tests markers` (file `<name>.md`).
- `--check` writes to a temporary directory with the same code path as the write mode, then compares every shard byte for byte with `--out` and reports the first difference as `stale: <shard>`; a shard missing from `--out` is `missing: <shard>`; a file in `--out` named `*.md` other than `MAP.md` and the eight shards is `unknown shard: <file>`; then `check_map`.
- `check_map` rules (each failure is exit 1 with one line naming it): `MAP.md` exists in `--out`; every backticked token in it that starts with `src/`, `tests/`, `build/`, `docs/` or `.github/`, contains no space, `{`, `*`, `<` or `...`, must exist under `--root` (file or directory); every shard file name appears in `MAP.md`; `MAP.md` is at most 120 lines.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test** in `build/scripts/tests/project-index.test.sh`, in the style of `dead-reference-check.test.sh` (read its helpers first: `must`, `make_tree`, `put`, `assert_eq`, `assert_contains`, `run_check`, `run_case`, the final `for c in …; do run_case "$c"; done`, output `ok: <case>: <what>`, final line `project-index: passed`). Cases for this task: `case_usage_errors` (unknown argument, `--root` without value, `--check` with a missing `--root` directory: exit 2); `case_markers_shard` (fixture with a `.cs` file holding `//#if (notifications)` … `//#endif`, a `.md` file holding `<!--#if (includeSample)-->` and a prose line quoting `` `//#if (x)` `` inline, a `.yml` with a bare `#if (caching == "redis")` line indented two spaces: expected rows exactly `| a.cs | //#if | notifications |`, `| b.md | <!--#if | includeSample |`, `| c.yml | #if | caching == "redis" |`, and no row for the prose line; `Rows: 3`); `case_determinism` (two runs, identical bytes, one fixture file saved with CRLF line endings, output identical to the same file with LF); `case_untracked_ignored` (a git fixture with a tracked marker file and an untracked marker file: only the tracked one is listed); `case_check_stale` (shard text altered: `--check` exit 1, output contains `stale: markers`); `case_check_missing_and_unknown` (a deleted shard gives `missing:`; an extra `x.md` gives `unknown shard: x.md`); `case_map_rules` (a `MAP.md` naming a path that does not exist exits 1 naming it; a shard not named in `MAP.md` exits 1; 121 lines exits 1; a valid one exits 0; a token with `{` is ignored). Fixtures build the other seven shard sources as empty trees where `need_rows` must not fire: Task 1 only requires the markers shard to be non-fatal on zero rows (a tree with no markers writes `Rows: 0`; zero rows is an error only for the sources named in Tasks 2 to 5).

Strip `\r` from every line read. Make it executable in git.

Expected: `Rows: 59`; the kinds and expressions of P2; no row for `docs/adr/0035-*` or `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-template-switches.md`; the run finishes in under 5 seconds on Git Bash (report the time).

### Task 2: Routes shard

**Files:**
- Modify: `build/scripts/project-index.sh` (`emit_routes`), `build/scripts/tests/project-index.test.sh`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 1.
- Produces: `routes.md`, columns `module | method | route | handler | permission | file`, route is the full path (`/api/v1/auth/mfa/…`), permission is the `RequirePermission(<Const>)` argument, or `anonymous` (`AllowAnonymous()`), or `authenticated` (`RequireAuthorization()`), handler is the first generic argument of the `ICommandHandler<…>` or `IQueryHandler<…>` parameter of the method named in the `MapX(route, Method)` call, or `-` when the method has none (JWKS).

- [ ] **Step 2: Run, expect red.**
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `emit_routes`** as a two-pass awk over `src/Modules/*/*/Endpoints/*Endpoints.cs` (found through `list_files`, so only tracked files): pass 1 records every `var X = Y.MapGroup("p")` (parent group `Y`, resolved to the Host `/api/v1` base when `Y` is the app, `api` or a variable assigned from the Host group), every `X.MapFooEndpoints();` call (caller group `X`) and every `Map…Endpoints(this RouteGroupBuilder P)` extension (its parameter name `P` takes the caller's prefix); pass 2 resolves `X.Map(Get|Post|Put|Patch|Delete)("route", Method)` (route may be a `const string` name in the same file) by joining prefix and route, removing a trailing `/` and any `//`; the permission is read from the chained calls up to the terminating `;`. Report any mismatch as a defect of the parser, not of the docs.

- Consumes: Tasks 1 to 5.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write `MAP.md`** (at most 120 lines, stable facts only: no counts, no lists of module or event names that change). Sections: how to use this index in three lines (start here, read at most one shard, shards are generated); the rule I7 verbatim at the top (after changing a route, permission, error code, event, job, configuration key, test folder or switch marker, run `bash build/scripts/project-index.sh` and commit the result; CI fails when stale); layout (one line each for `src/Modules/<Name>/` and its folders `Domain Application Infrastructure Endpoints Resources`, `src/BuildingBlocks`, `src/Host`, `tests/*`, `build/scripts`, `.github/workflows`, `docs/`); naming and path conventions an agent needs to guess a path (`*Endpoints.cs`, `*Permissions.cs`, `*Errors.cs`, `*IntegrationEvent`, `*Job.cs`, `SectionName`, tests mirror modules by folder); a "where to look for what" table sending each of the spec's eight lookups to one shard and naming the module doc section that holds the prose; pitfalls (generated files are not edited; markers are comments in the all-on tree, only on-only regions, never `#else`; a merge conflict in a shard is resolved by regenerating; the template files `docs/README.md` and the ADR tables are tested elsewhere).
